subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A drawback of relying only on extrinsic motivation, such as rewards, is that:
options: It builds long-lasting love of the sport
Performers always enjoy the sport more
The performer may lose interest once the reward is removed
questions.explain: If a performer is driven only by rewards, their motivation can fall away once those rewards stop.

questions.q: Blood doping is a banned method that works by:
options: Increasing red blood cells to carry more oxygen
Reducing the number of red blood cells
questions.explain: Blood doping raises the red blood cell count so more oxygen can be delivered to the muscles, boosting endurance.

questions.q: The sit-and-reach test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility, particularly of the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: Which is a possible emotional consequence of a sedentary lifestyle?
options: Increased risk of depression and low self-esteem
questions.explain: A sedentary lifestyle can lower self-esteem and increase the risk of depression and stress.

questions.q: A pie chart is most useful for showing:
options: Change in heart rate over time
Proportions of a whole, such as percentage of training time per method
questions.explain: Pie charts show how a whole is divided into proportions or percentages.

questions.q: A long-term effect of resistance training on the muscular system is:
questions.explain: Regular resistance training causes muscle hypertrophy, an increase in the size and strength of muscle fibres.

questions.q: Using the formula 220 - age, what is the maximum heart rate of a 16-year-old?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 16 = 204 bpm.

questions.q: In periodisation, the phase just before the competitive season that sharpens skills and fitness is the:
questions.explain: The pre-season phase builds specific fitness and sharpens skills ready for competition.

questions.q: Which muscle is the antagonist when the hamstrings contract to flex the knee?
questions.explain: The quadriceps act as the antagonist, relaxing and lengthening while the hamstrings flex the knee.

questions.q: Which is an example of qualitative data?
options: A coach's description of a player's attitude
A player's sprint time in seconds
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and subjective, such as a coach's observations of attitude or technique.

questions.q: A coach's written opinion on a player's effort is an example of:
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and based on opinions, judgements or observations.

questions.q: The traditional Borg RPE scale runs from:
questions.explain: The original Borg scale runs from 6 to 20, where the value roughly relates to heart rate when multiplied by ten.

questions.q: What is the maximum heart rate of a 15-year-old using the standard formula?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 15 = 205 bpm.

questions.q: What does the 'M' in SMART goal setting stand for?
questions.explain: In SMART targets the M stands for Measurable, so progress can be tracked.

questions.q: Which strategy is commonly used to reduce football hooliganism?
options: Encouraging standing terraces with no segregation
questions.explain: All-seater stadia, CCTV, segregation of fans and alcohol controls help reduce spectator violence.

questions.q: A benefit of sponsorship for a performer is that it:
options: Provides funding for equipment, coaching and travel
questions.explain: Sponsorship provides financial support that helps athletes afford training, coaching and competition.

questions.q: How would you calculate a 40-year-old's estimated maximum heart rate?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 - age, so 220 - 40 = 180 bpm.

questions.q: Why is it useful to collect data when analysing performance?
options: It replaces the need for skill
It gives objective evidence to identify strengths and weaknesses
questions.explain: Data provides objective evidence to identify strengths and weaknesses and to set targets.

questions.q: A skill made up of many subroutines that requires concentration and decision-making is classified as a:
questions.explain: Complex skills involve many subroutines and require attention, judgement and decision-making.

questions.q: Hawk-Eye technology is mainly used in sport to:
options: Aid officials in making accurate decisions
questions.explain: Hawk-Eye helps officials make accurate decisions on close calls, improving fairness.

questions.q: A goal that is too difficult and unrealistic is most likely to:
options: Lower motivation and confidence if it is not met
Have no effect on the performer
questions.explain: Unrealistic goals can demotivate a performer and reduce confidence when they are not achieved.

questions.q: Which type of feedback is given by an external source such as a coach or scoreboard?
questions.explain: Extrinsic feedback comes from an outside source such as a coach, teammate or scoreboard.
